title: Supreme Court decision: Federal Reserve cutout
framing: Trump v. Slaughter — The Court further overturned a 91-year-old precedent that prevented presidents from removing members of independent agencies at will. In a 6-3 ruling, the justices found that Trump's firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter without cause was lawful, a major expansion of executive power.

LF.text: The FTC exists to protect people from monopolies and fraud, and that protection only works if the commissioners enforcing it can't be fired for doing their jobs.

LC.text: We stand with Slaughter because independent watchdogs belong to the people, not to whoever sits in the Oval Office.

LD.text: The president doesn't remove commissioners — he removes *obstacles*.

RF.text: The FTC exists to protect people from monopolies and fraud, and that protection only works if the commissioners can do their jobs without fearing the President will fire them for it.

RC.text: We stand together to protect the agencies that protect us.

RD.text: The agencies were never truly independent — they were always ours to direct.
